name: The AI Hippocampus (TMLR survey)
ontology_notes: Map, not an engine. Taxonomy is implicit (parametric Transformer memory, FFN key-value, knowledge neurons, Hopfield-style association, ROME/MEMIT editing, unlearning), explicit (external RAG over text, vectors, graphs/triples, long-context indexes), and agentic (STM in the context window, LTM as facts, trajectories, user feedback, dialogues and personalization, plus multi-agent shared stores). §5 adds multimodal and embodied memory. Companion holes are not taxonomy axes. Repo bigai-nlco/LLM-Memory-Survey is LICENSE, empty README.md, and memory.png.

ontology.evidence: Survey taxonomy in §1 and Figure 1. Implicit, explicit, agentic. Not a store with user bio, character autobiography, relationship, lore, or OOC types.
ontology.label: measured

write_policy.evidence: No ingest pipeline of their own. §4.1 reviews recall-then-write agent loops from other papers. §7 says they do not propose a platform that integrates the mechanisms.
write_policy.label: measured

read_policy.evidence: Explicit memory is reviewed as retrieve-then-generate RAG (§3). Agentic LTM is reviewed as retrieve before acting (§4.1). No skip-relevant-hit policy.
read_policy.label: measured

supersession.evidence: §2.2 reviews parametric editing and unlearning. §4.4 names variance and knowledge utilization as literature metrics. The survey does not implement invalidate-or-replace.
supersession.label: measured

temporal.evidence: §4.4 lists temporality as a qualitative axis and temporal reasoning as a low-level metric from Wu et al. 2024a. No validity-window store.
temporal.label: measured

identity_split.evidence: Personalization examples are one user plus one assistant (MemoryBank/SiliconFriend in §4.1.2). No user vs character vs relationship split.
identity_split.label: measured

silence.evidence: §7 future work is Transformer internals, long context vs RAG, dynamic adaptation, multimodal tokens. No trauma, kink, or spoiler skip.
silence.label: measured

poisoning.evidence: Parametric unlearning of harmful training knowledge is reviewed in §2.2. Stored-chat jailbreaks that overwrite a companion persona are not a surveyed defense.
poisoning.label: measured

forgetting.evidence: Reviews Ebbinghaus-style agent decay and knowledge unlearning as other people's methods (§2.2, §4.1.2). No forget-that engine and no next-turn derived-row check.
forgetting.label: measured

cost_shape.evidence: §4.4.2 names latency and API token cost as general agent metrics. No per-turn extract/retrieve budget for a companion.
cost_shape.label: measured

local.evidence: MIT LICENSE in bigai-nlco/LLM-Memory-Survey. Tree is LICENSE, empty README, memory.png. Not a local memory runtime.
local.label: measured

mcp.evidence: No MCP server in the paper or the survey repo.
mcp.label: measured

companion_fit_reason: TMLR survey. Useful map of implicit, explicit, and agentic memory plus multimodal work. It is not a system. §7 states they do not ship a unified eval or an integrating platform. Companion silence, typed writers, lore vs lived event, and stored-text persona poisoning are not coverage axes.

published_eval.what_it_actually_scores: Survey. Table 4 reprints correctness and latency for other memory frameworks on Llama3-8B-IT. Those are not scores of an AI Hippocampus engine. §4.4 reviews NarrativeQA, NIAH, ALFWorld, WebArena, AgentBench, and Wu-style IE/MR/KU/TR/ABS metrics. None are companion silence, identity drift, or typed-writer retcon.

open_unknowns: HTML fetch of arxiv.org/html/2601.09113 timed out once. The abs HTML dump and GitHub repo were used. TMLR journal reference is 11/2025 on the abs page.
README.md in LLM-Memory-Survey is empty. Paper also cites the same URL as the survey website.
